# Provenance: design/HIGHER-ORDER-FUNCTIONS.0.md §1 ("What works — the

# programs were transcripts — run on audit days, quoted verbatim, and
# re-checked only when someone re-ran the note. These rows make the §1
# evidence a standing gate: the interpreter oracle re-checks every value on
# every `make test`, and the compile ledger (frontier_spec_test.go) pins
# which programs the compiler still refuses and why — mostly the audit's
# §5.8 "body result of unknown provenance" class over curried combinator

# the rows that def-bind a COMPUTED fn (`def fact (fgen fgen/v)`,
# `def h (compose …)`) refuse one stage earlier, at check diagnostics.
# NUR089 (the inline-lambda call site) is a CLI-check property of the B
# row, noted in its description — the compile lane refuses that row in
# the provenance class before the check shape matters. Graduation per
# row = the refusal clears → delete its ledger entry.
# The §1.4 divergences — Z, and the naive Y no strict language can run —
# are NOT pinned: no budget bounds them (a 200 000-step CLI budget ran 30 s
# without tripping, and an in-process run is eventually killed by memory),
# so a test would hang the suite. What IS pinned is the deterministic §5.4
# application-context rule that makes Z's λv guard inert — the §7 rows.

column1: # §5  a real parser-combinator library (audit §1.5). All four rows draw the
#     NUR087 checker false positive (branch-local def after a call through a
#     Function parameter), so the compile lane refuses at check; the
#     interpreter is the oracle that the library WORKS.

def pitem s:String => [ if (eq 0 (size s)) [ {ok:false rest:s val:None} ] [ {ok:true val:(slice 0 1 s) rest:(slice 1 (size s) s)} ] ] end def psat fn p:Function Function [ ( fn s:String Map [ def r (pitem s) if (r.ok) [ if (p (r.val)) [ r ] [ {ok:false rest:s val:None} ] ] [ r ] ] ) ] end def manyloop fn [[a:Function s:String acc:List][Map][ def r (a s) if (r.ok) [ (manyloop a/v (r.rest) (push (r.val) acc)) ] [ {ok:true val:acc rest:s} ] ]] end def pmany fn a:Function Function [ ( fn s:String Map [ def z [] (manyloop a/v s z) ] ) ] end def isdigit c:String => [ and (gte "0" c) (lte "9" c) ] end def digit (psat isdigit/v) end def digits (pmany digit/v) end (digits '123ab')
column3: many(sat(digit)) consumes the digit prefix

column1: # §9b the §4.3 capture-reachability fallback (2026-08-21): a call of a
#     def-bound factory closure whose unit carries construction-scope
#     captures lowers as a fn-VALUE apply through the def site's
#     operand (RecordDynApplyName) — the runtime closure's baked
#     captures apply VM-native. Repeats, rebinds and multi-instance
#     spellings all compile; per-call outs freshen (the memoised
#     residual shares IDs — without it `(h 5) (h 10)` compiled [17 17]).

column1: # §9d the GRADUAL inner parameter (2026-08-21): the same
#     apply-the-capture factory as §9b/§9, but the inner lambda's
#     parameter is Any rather than a concrete type. The window is
#     otherwise identical and its lead is admitted — only the
#     ARGUMENT gate refuses, because a gradual argument cannot be
#     proven non-function and the interpreter RAISES on a
#     function-valued one (its leading collection meets a barrier)
#     where the trailing model applies. Refuses; ledgered. There is
#     no runtime repair: the raise is a property of word dispatch,
#     so an island over the resolved window leaves both values inert.
#     This is the Church chain's actual blocker (§5.8 stage 1).
def app g:Function => [x:Any => [(g x)]] end def h (app (z:Integer => [add 7 z])) end (h 5)
column3: the arrow-inner factory with a gradual inner parameter (refuses; ledgered)

column1: # §9e the curried CHAIN through def bindings (2026-08-21): a
#     three-level factory whose intermediate results are each
#     def-bound. `def f2 (f1 2)` binds f2 to the very carrier f1
#     denotes — the analysis cannot model the apply, so it returns
#     the callee unchanged — and compiled that bound both names to
#     ONE slot and leaked the unconsumed argument into the residual
#     (`2 fn (Integer) 3` for the interpreter's `6`). A REGRESSION
#     introduced by the Stage 1 read substitution: before it the
#     read raised undefined_word and the program refused. Now the
#     def site detects the dropped apply and refuses. Ledgered.
def mk2 fn [[a:Integer][Function][( fn [[b:Integer][Function][( fn [[c:Integer][Integer][add a (add b c)]] )]] )]] end def f1 (mk2 1) end def f2 (f1 2) end (f2 3)
column3: the three-level curried chain through def bindings (refuses; ledgered)
